extracted.intended_audience: plant breeders, agricultural businesses, researchers, and others seeking or advising on plant variety protection under U.S. law
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes the statutory eligibility standards and practical guidance for obtaining a Plant Variety Protection Act (PVPA) certificate in the United States — i.e., what a breeder must show about a new plant variety. Useful to breeders preparing applications and advisors assessing eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: The plant variety must be new and not previously available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate that the variety has not been commercially available or otherwise released prior to the application. Collect documentation and evidence of breeding history, release dates, and any public disclosures. Example given: a newly developed tomato variety resistant to certain diseases that was not previously available could meet novelty. Reference: Plant Variety Protection Act, codified at 7 U.S.C. § 2321 et seq.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: The variety must be clearly distinguishable from existing varieties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show specific, identifiable characteristics that differentiate the candidate variety from all known, relevant existing varieties (morphological traits, disease resistance, growth habit, etc.). Examples: a new hybrid flower that is distinct from all existing varieties. Provide comparative descriptions and evidence demonstrating clear differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniformity
rubrics_metrics.description: The variety must be uniform in its characteristics when propagated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide data and observations showing that plants of the variety exhibit consistent, predictable traits under normal propagation. Breeding records, trial data, and propagation test results can demonstrate uniformity. Explain how the variety behaves when propagated (e.g., through seed or vegetative means) and the degree of acceptable variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability
rubrics_metrics.description: The variety must maintain its traits over time and through propagation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document multi-generation trials or other evidence that the distinguishing characteristics remain stable across successive propagations. Provide records of tests demonstrating trait stability and how the variety preserves its defining features after repeated propagation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term and scope of protection (legal element)
rubrics_metrics.description: PVPA grants exclusive rights to breeders for a limited statutory term (generally 25 years for most crops under the PVPA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand the legal consequences and limits of protection: the certificate confers exclusive rights to sell and reproduce the protected variety for the statutory period; infringement can give rise to legal action and financial penalties. Compare with related forms of protection: plant patents (typically 20 years) protect specific varieties differently, while trademarks protect brand identity rather than genetic traits. Cite: 7 U.S.C. § 2321 et seq.
